parties.petitioner_plaintiff: CHHATTAR SINGH, S/O SHRI KANCHAN SINGH KUSHWAH, AGED 53 YEARS, OCCUPATION: AGRICULTURE.
parties.respondent_defendant: SURENDRA KUMAR S/O DEEPCHAND KUSHWAHA, AGED 25 YEARS, OCCUPATION: LABOUR

facts_of_case: The present Petitioners moved an application for mutation of their names in the revenue records u/s 109-110 of M.P. Land Revenue Code with regard to certain lands.

legal_principles.principle: On the basis of WILL, mutation cannot be done by revenue authorities.
legal_principles.held: It was contended that a WILL was also executed in their by their Grandfather Daulatram and hiding all these facts and without making the Respondents party in the mutation proceedings got their names mutated in the revenue records on the basis of WILL, which was illegal and was against the settled principle of law.

legal_principles.principle: Children born out of the company cannot be said to be illegitimate children.
legal_principles.held: It was also contended that even as per provisions of section 16 of Hindu Marriage Act, such children has a right in the property and therefore, without making them as a party in the mutation proceedings, the mutation of the names of the Petitioner in the revenue records on the basis of WILL, which was illegal and was against the settled principle of law.

outcome.final_order: The order passed by the Sub-Divisional-Officer was affirmed.

keywords: Latin maxim: 'Nemo dat quod non habet'
